sections.eyebrow: The shape we look for first
sections.h2: Rankings earned. Clicks parked on page two.
lines: Most clicks go to the top three results. A site can rank for a thousand keywords and still not grow, because its rankings sit at positions 4 to 20, where almost nobody clicks.
That is not solved by publishing more. It is a foundations problem, and the cheapest growth a mature site has.
sections.caption: Organic search symptoms, with the direct cause and the deeper cause behind each
head: What you see
Direct cause
Deeper cause, the one that brings it back
rows: Keywords stuck at positions 11 to 20
The page answers the query only partly, and few internal links point at it.
Trusted sites link to the home page, not to the pages that earn money.
Two pages trading one keyword
Duplicate pages for one intent: due dates, calculators, addresses.
No page has one clear job, so Google splits the signal and neither wins.
High impressions, low click-through
Titles and descriptions that do not carry the offer.
The proof that sells (price, speed, credentials) lives on the page, not in the result.
Blog traffic that never converts
Topics picked by search volume.
Posts do not feed a service page, so traffic arrives and leaves.
A monthly report with no explanation
Numbers without the action behind them.
Nobody links what changed on the site to what moved in search.
sections.note: Every problem gets two answers. Fixing only the first is why the same problem is back six months later.

sections.h2: Fix the foundations. Then grow on top.
lines: New content on a site Google half understands compounds slowly. The same content on a clean site compounds fast.

items.t: Page by page: indexing, duplicates, internal links, schema, backlinks and an AI-answer baseline. Working, not working and why, agreed with your team.
Duplicates merged behind 301s, one keyword owner per page, titles rewritten to carry the proof, links pointed at the pages that earn.
A schema framework: organization, product, pricing, FAQ, how-to and article, with the same facts stated the same way everywhere.
Page-two keywords first, because they are closest to paying. Content in clusters that feed one service page. Links earned, never bought in spikes.
When the year's demand lands in a few weeks, month on month is noise. We compare year on year, and build before the peak so you enter it already ranking.

items.h: Commodity products near the price floor
items.t: When the product is the same everywhere, search is where share is won: one price stated once, trust in the result itself, and an answer for every question the leader answers and you do not.

items.h: A network of sites and an in-house team
items.t: We own the sites we are given, and write every tactic that works as a playbook with the return it produced, so your team can run it across the rest of the portfolio.

sections.eyebrow: How an engine chooses a brand to name
sections.h2: Four signals, and what we build for each.
sections.caption: What AI engines look for when naming a brand, and the work that answers it
head: What the engine looks for
What we build
rows: A clear answer it can quote
Answer-first blocks of 40 to 60 words, numbered steps, tables of deadlines, rates and penalties.
Facts it can trust
FAQ, how-to, organization and pricing schema, with one price and one set of facts across every site you run.
Other sites that mention you
Mentions where buyers ask: Reddit, trade forums, Quora, YouTube how-tos, trade media.
The pages it already cites
The pages the engines quote for your topics, including the best-provider lists your competitors wrote, and a place on them.

sections.h2: An AI answer changes every time. So we ask many times.
lines: One screenshot proves nothing. CitedSpy asks the same questions across engines, again and again, and reports the average.

sections.h2: In a trust-led category, a penalty costs more than it gains.
lines: No private blog networks, no paid link farms, no bulk directories, no spikes. Every link sits inside relevant content on a site your buyers read, aimed at the page that needs the authority, and reported with its URL, target, anchor and live date.
And no promised rankings or AI placements. We commit to the work, and show what it moved.
